newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Stad R'dam sees 96 profit up 12-20 pct.
newsitem.headline: Stad R'dam sees 96 profit up 12-20 pct.

text.p: Dutch insurer Stad Rotterdam Anno 1720 NV said on Wednesday its 1996 net profit would be 12 to 20 percent higher than the 133.4 million guilders of 1995.
"The rise in profits in 1996 will be 12 to 20 percent," Stad Rotterdam chairman Carlo de Swart told Reuters in an interview.
Last November the medium sized insurer said it expected a significant rise in full-year net profit and a clear increase in full-year earnings per share compared with 1995.
The group's net profit rose 11.7 over the first quarter of 1996, 13 percent over the first six months of 1996 and 15.6 percent over the first three quarters of 1996.
De Swart said 1996 pre-tax profit was expected to rise to 227 million guilders from 196 million guilders in 1995.
"We base those estimates on the figures we announced after the first three quarters of 1996," De Swart said.

He said pre-tax life insurance profits were expected to rise to 115 million guilders in 1996 from 106 million in 1995 while pre-tax non-life profits were expected to rise to 112 million guilders in 1996 from 90 million in 1995.
"Health and accident is doing extremely well," De Swart said, adding that non-life had made an excellent recovery.
De Swart said motor insurance would show a modest profit again after losses in the previous two years.
"Motor insurance will return to profit. I'm quite sure of that," he said. "We would be happy to make a profit of one or two percent on our motor portfolio," he added.
Premium-income on car insurance was expected to be around 380-400 million guilders in 1996.
In 1995 the company made a gross loss of 15.5 million guilders on its motor business which followed a gross loss of 33.2 million guilders in 1994.
"We hope car insurance will go well for some more years," De Swart said, noting that this sector was notoriously cyclical.

Stad Rotterdam estimates that new business in mortgages increased by 25 percent in 1996 to about 2.0 billion guilders, from 1.6 billion guilders in 1995, but this remained below the 1994 peak of 2.4 billion guilders.

Turning to life business, De Swart said the production of regular-premium life policies had increased by about 20 percent in 1996, but single-premium policies had stayed at about the same level as in 1995.
De Swart said for the time being at least Stad Rotterdam would stick to its long-standing official target of increasing profits by an average of at least seven percent annually.
But he conceded that this was "not very exciting" and said the company would in fact aim higher. "The ambition is to show double digit growth," he said.
